rationale: The bid-ask spread is excessively wide at 82.3 bps ($0.18), representing nearly a third of the 5-minute ATR and creating prohibitive friction for entry and stop execution. Furthermore, the portfolio already carries heavy long exposure (42.9% of buying power across seven long commitments) while nearly half of the daily loss budget has been consumed. Going short against an extreme market-wide rally (SPY +5.33%) and strong relative volume (3.33x) near session highs offers poor expectancy, while buying the high into an illiquid spread degrades the risk-reward profile.
